claim_verdicts.evidence: stage-1 scripts/dev-secrets.sh:16-23 is exactly the block quoted: if ! grep -q '^JWT_SIGNING_KEY=' .env ... echo "JWT_SIGNING_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 48)" >> .env. Live lab: the value after JWT_SIGNING_KEY= in .env is 64 characters (counted with wc -c, value not printed) = base64 of 48 bytes.

Program.cs:23-24 `builder.Configuration["Jwt:SigningKey"] ?? throw` fires only when the value is null. docker-compose.yml sets Jwt__SigningKey: "${JWT_SIGNING_KEY}"; Docker docs: "If an environment variable is not set, Compose substitutes with an empty string." Live: JWT_SIGNING_KEY= docker compose up -d api -> container stays Up, printenv shows Jwt__SigningKey empty, requests fail with System.ArgumentException IDX10703. Rest verified: IssuerSigningKey, ValidateIssuerSigningKey, JwtTokenService.cs:15-16 HmacSha256 on the same setting.
claim_verdicts.source: stage-1 Program.cs:22-41, JwtTokenService.cs:15-16, docker-compose.yml:92; refs/docker-docs .../variable-interpolation.md:273; live run
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Program.cs lines 22-41 read Jwt:SigningKey (throwing at startup only if the setting is absent; an empty value passes and requests then fail) and set IssuerSigningKey to a SymmetricSecurityKey from it with ValidateIssuerSigningKey; JwtTokenService signs with the same Jwt:SigningKey (HmacSha256).

claim_verdicts.evidence: As a general statement "Configuration is read at startup" is contradicted by the aspnetcore docs: "the appsettings.json and appsettings.{ENVIRONMENT}.json files are enabled with reloadOnChange set to true, which means that changes made to [them] after the app starts take effect immediately". It holds here because Program.cs:23 copies the value once into `signingKey` before building TokenValidationParameters, and the value comes from an environment variable of the container process. Live: the key changed only by recreating the container.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Program.cs copies Jwt:SigningKey once at startup into the token validation settings, and the value comes from an environment variable fixed when the container starts, so a changed signing key takes effect only when the API starts again.

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 8725 sec. 2.2: "Some applications use a keyed Message Authentication Code (MAC) algorithm, such as 'HS256', to sign tokens but supply a weak symmetric key with insufficient entropy (such as a human-memorable password). Such keys are vulnerable to offline brute-force or dictionary attacks once an attacker gets hold of such a token." Forgery by any key holder: Program.cs validates only by recomputing with IssuerSigningKey (plus iss/aud/exp, all readable from a real token); no token store exists in stage-1.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725 sec. 2.2; rfc7518 sec. 3.2; stage-1 Program.cs:22-41

claim_verdicts.evidence: Live run: login -> token; POST /api/v1/orders -> 201. After JWT_SIGNING_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 48) docker compose up -d api: 502 for ~3 s, then 401 with the same token. After docker compose up -d api: 502 for ~3 s, then 201 (order 35, status new) with the same token. Token lifetime is 8 h (JwtTokenService.cs:28 AddHours(8)), so the restore works only within that window.

Docker docs: "when the same variable is declared by multiple sources, precedence applies: 1. Variables from your shell environment 2. ... --env-file 3. ... .env file". Live output: "Container donhang-api Recreate / Recreated / Starting / Started" for both commands; after the restore the container's key hash equals the .env key hash. App: create_order_screen.dart sets 'Failed: $e' and api_client.dart:55 throws Exception('failed to create order (${response.statusCode})'), so a 401 renders "Failed: Exception: failed to create order (401)".

Follows from claim 4 and the code: OrdersController identity comes from the token's sub, so a forged sub acts as any customer; nothing in Program.cs depends on where the request comes from. RFC 8725 sec. 3.5: "Human-memorizable passwords MUST NOT be directly used as the key to a keyed-MAC algorithm such as 'HS256'."

issues.text: Prose does not describe what this code does on the lab's own path. `?? throw` catches only a null value. Compose's `Jwt__SigningKey: "${JWT_SIGNING_KEY}"` turns a missing .env line into an empty string, which passes the check: run live, the container stays Up and every request fails with IDX10703. A learner told the API 'refuses to start' will look for a crashed container that is not there.
issues.quote: reads the key like any other setting, and the API refuses to start without it
issues.fix: Replace the clause with: "reads the key like any other setting, and throws at startup if the setting is missing altogether." Or drop "and the API refuses to start without it". Update claim 2 with the suggested_text.

issues.text: Unlisted claims: (a) "`.gitignore` keeps both out of the repository", (b) "Compose passes it as `Jwt__SigningKey`" (also in the diagram and summary line 2). Neither is in the ledger. Both are true at stage-1 (.gitignore line 1 is `.env`; docker-compose.yml:92 `Jwt__SigningKey: "${JWT_SIGNING_KEY}"`).
issues.quote: The key is in `.env` next to `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, and `.gitignore` keeps both out of the repository.
issues.fix: Leave the text as written. Add two `fact` claims (section 5) with source_hint `examples/don-hang @ stage-1: .gitignore:1` and `docker-compose.yml:92`.

issues.text: Overstated: the API does not accept every token its key would have signed. Program.cs also checks issuer, audience and lifetime (ValidateIssuer/Audience/Lifetime = true). The Try-it answer repeats the overstatement. An old token matches again after a restore only if its 8-hour lifetime (JwtTokenService.cs:28) has not run out.
issues.quote: the API accepts exactly the tokens its current key would have signed
issues.fix: In section 4, change it to "the API accepts only tokens its current key would have signed". In the section 7 answer, change "the check depends only on the key and the token" to "the signature check depends only on the key and the token, and the token had not expired yet".

issues.text: Live run of steps 3 and 5: for about 3 seconds after each `docker compose up -d api`, POST /api/v1/orders through Caddy returned 502 before it returned 401 or 201. A learner who taps quickly sees "failed to create order (502)", which is not the expected result.
issues.quote: After a few seconds, tap "Order 1 keyboard" in the browser.
issues.fix: Say "Wait about ten seconds, then tap...", and in Expected result add: "(502) means the API is still starting; tap again." Apply the same to step 5.

issues.text: The summary says the script writes 48 random bytes into .env. It actually writes their 64-character base64 text, and the API signs with the UTF-8 bytes of that text. Section 5 already describes this correctly, so the summary contradicts it.
issues.fix: "`scripts/dev-secrets.sh` writes a key made from 48 random bytes, as base64 text, into `.env`, next to `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`."

issues.text: Explanation d is false for this stack. Live run with JWT_SIGNING_KEY=donhang: login fails and the log shows "IDX10653: The encryption algorithm 'HS256' requires a key size of at least '128' bits". An empty key fails with IDX10703. The key (c) is still correct. The stem's example key `donhang` could not be used in this lab at all, but the statement is still false.
issues.quote: The API accepts any text as the key; it is up to the setup to make it long and random.
issues.fix: en d: "The API has no rule about real words; its library only rejects keys too short for HMAC-SHA256, and making the key long and random is up to the setup." Mirror in vi. Optionally make the stem's example a longer memorable phrase, e.g. `donhang-secret-key-2026`.

I cannot narrate the diagram in order after reading section 4.

issues.text: The same key has three names: JWT_SIGNING_KEY in .env, Jwt__SigningKey passed by Compose, and Jwt:SigningKey read in Program.cs. Nothing tells me why the double underscore becomes a colon, or that these are the same setting. Core concepts states it ('which the API reads as Jwt:SigningKey') but not why, so I would doubt the code reads the value Compose sets.
issues.quote: Compose passes it to the API as `Jwt__SigningKey`, and `Program.cs` reads it at startup:
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this line: "ASP.NET Core reads a double underscore in an environment variable name as the colon in a setting name, so Jwt__SigningKey arrives as Jwt:SigningKey."

issues.text: The Program.cs block uses names I have never seen and the prose does not place: AddJwtBearer, JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme, TokenValidationParameters, SymmetricSecurityKey, MapInboundClaims, ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier, OrdersController.
